---
title: "Match bending modulus"
format: html
---

We want to make a model of a fish with an oval cross section that matches the bending modulus of the thin plastic panels that Alyx Khuat-Sherwood used when she was testing the effect of tail shape.

# Alyx's foils

Bending modulus is $EI$ where $E$ is the Young's modulus of the material and $I$ is the second moment of area of the cross-section of the material.

![Experimental set up. A) Foil held in place by a coupler inserted with a rod. B) Force transducer connected to the foil by a metal rod. C) Motor connected to the force transducer with a rod and mounted to 80-20 scaffolding. D) Foil silhouettes.](AlyxFoils.png)

## Young's modulus

The foils are made of PETG plastic. According to [McMaster](https://www.mcmaster.com/products/plastic?s=petg%20plastic), it has a tensile stiffness of 7100 psi.

```{r}
E_PETG.psi <- 7100
psi2Pa <- 6895        # N/m^2 per psi
E_PETG.Pa <- E_PETG.psi * psi2Pa

E_PETG.Pa / 1e6
```

## Second moment of area

Alyx's foils were 0.4mm thick. The rectangular foil had a length of 19cm and an area of 36.61cm\^2, so its height is 1.93cm.

Second moment of area for a [rectangular cross section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_second_moments_of_area) is

$$\frac{w^3 h}{12}$$

```{r}
L.mm <- 190
w.mm <- 0.4
h.mm <- 19.3
I.mm4 <- w.mm^3 * h.mm / 12

I.mm4
```

## Bending modulus

Convert the units and multiply things out

```{r}
mm2m <- (1 / 1000)   # m per mm
EI_Alyx <- E_PETG.Pa * (I.mm4 * mm2m^4)

EI_Alyx
```

# Match with an oval cross section

The softest material we can print has a Young's modulus of 0.278MPa. If we want an oval cross section, with height the same as Alyx's foils, then how wide can they be to match her bending modulus?

```{r}
E_print.Pa <- 0.278e6
```

Second moment of area for an oval is $$ \frac{\pi}{4} w^3 h $$

So if we have $$ EI_{oval} = EI_{Alyx} $$

$$ \tfrac{\pi}{4} E_{print} w_{oval}^3 h = EI_{Alyx} $$

$$ w_{oval} = \left( \frac{4 EI_{Alyx}}{\pi E_{print} h} \right)^{1/3} $$

```{r}
w_oval.m <- ((4 * EI_Alyx) / (pi * E_print.Pa * (h.mm/1000)))^(1/3)

w_oval.mm <- w_oval.m * 1000
w_oval.mm
```

What if we reduce the height?

```{r}
w_ovalh2.m <- ((4 * EI_Alyx) / (pi * E_print.Pa * (h.mm/1000/2)))^(1/3)

w_ovalh2.mm <- w_ovalh2.m * 1000
w_ovalh2.mm
```

Doesn't change things much.

What material would we need to have a 10mm thick oval? $$ E = EI_{Alyx} / I_{10} $$

```{r}
I_10.mm4 <- pi/4 * (10^3) * (h.mm)
I_10.m4 <- I_10.mm4 * (mm2m^4)

E_new.Pa <- EI_Alyx / I_10.m4

E_new.Pa
```

```{r}
I_5.mm4 <- pi/4 * (5^3) * (h.mm)
I_5.m4 <- I_5.mm4 * (mm2m^4)

E_new.Pa <- EI_Alyx / I_5.m4

E_new.Pa
```

# Match effective flexibility

Effective flexibility is a measure from beam bending. Maybe we try to match that, instead of the exact bending modulus.

$$ \Pi = \left( \frac{\rho h L^5 \phi^2}{EI} \right)^{1/2} $$

where $h$ is height, $L$ is length, and $\phi$ is the bending frequency.

## Alyx's effective flexibility

Alyx tested her foils at 2Hz.

```{r}
rho.kgpm3 <- 1000    # kg per m^3
freq.Hz <- 2
Pi_Alyx <- sqrt(rho.kgpm3 * (h.mm / 1000) * (L.mm / 1000)^5 * freq.Hz^2 / EI_Alyx)

Pi_Alyx
```

Suppose we make a fish model with a thickness of 10mm.

```{r}
w_oval.mm <- 10
I_oval.mm4 <- pi/4 * w_oval.mm^3 * h.mm

I_oval.mm4
```

```{r}
EI_oval.Nm2 <- E_print.Pa * (I_oval.mm4 * mm2m^4)

EI_oval.Nm2
```

To match $Pi$ by varying $L$ we have

$$ \Pi_{oval} = \Pi_{Alyx} $$

$$ \frac{\rho h L_{oval}^5 \phi^2}{EI_{oval}} = \Pi_{Alyx}^2 $$

$$ L_{oval} = \left( \frac{ \Pi_{Alyx}^2 EI_{oval}} {\rho h \phi^2} \right)^{1/5} $$

Check units: $$ [m] = \left( \frac{[]^2 [N m^2]}{[kg / m^3] [m] [1/s]^2} \right)^{1/5} $$

$$ [m] = \left( \frac{[]^2 [kg m^3/s^2 ]}{[kg / m^2 / s^2] } \right)^{1/5} $$ $$ [m] = \left( m^5 \right) ^ {1/5} $$

```{r}
L_oval.m <- ((Pi_Alyx^2 * EI_oval.Nm2) / (rho.kgpm3 * (h.mm / 1000) * freq.Hz^2)) ^ (1/5)

L_oval.mm <- L_oval.m * 1000
L_oval.mm
```

What if we also increase frequency?

```{r}
freq_oval.Hz <- 4

L_oval.m <- ((Pi_Alyx^2 * EI_oval.Nm2) / (rho.kgpm3 * (h.mm / 1000) * freq_oval.Hz^2)) ^ (1/5)

L_oval.mm <- L_oval.m * 1000
L_oval.mm
```

Suppose we want a length of 20cm. What would the thickness be?

Then we have

$$ EI_{oval} = \frac{\rho h L_{oval}^5 \phi^2}{\Pi_{Alyx}^2} $$

$$ \tfrac{\pi}{4} E_{oval} w_{oval}^3 h = \frac{\rho h L_{oval}^5 \phi^2}{\Pi_{Alyx}^2} $$

$$ w_{oval} = \left( \frac{4 \rho L_{oval}^5 \phi^2}
{\pi \Pi_{Alyx}^2 E_{print}} \right)^{1/3} $$

```{r}
L_oval.m <- 0.20

w_oval.m <- ((4 * rho.kgpm3 * L_oval.m^5 * freq_oval.Hz^2) / (pi * Pi_Alyx^2 * (E_print.Pa))) ^ (1/3)

w_oval.mm <- w_oval.m * 1000
w_oval.mm
```
